name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do: Replace the current prompt-review system with a shared log that records every prompt change, who made it, and why. This makes decisions transparent and auditable without slowing down iteration. The trade-off is storage growth, but the clarity outweighs the cost.

name: Gauge
text: A shared log could create noise rather than clarity; it risks overwhelming users with irrelevant details and obscuring important decisions. Instead, implement a structured decision-making process that includes context summaries for each change, focusing on the reasons and impacts of decisions. To settle the argument, propose a pilot where you compare the shared log against a concise summary approach in terms of clarity and usability.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do: Add a lightweight "impact matrix" to the shared log that tracks prompt changes and their effects—like response quality shifts or latency impacts—with a one-line summary of the trade-off accepted. This keeps decisions auditable without drowning users in noise. The trade-off is upfront effort to define metrics, but it pays off by making future reviews faster and more reliable.

name: Gauge
text: A shared log with an impact matrix still risks becoming a graveyard of stale data—changes accumulate, but no one curates the matrix to prune irrelevant entries, so the signal decays into noise. Instead, enforce a rule: every logged change must include a "sunset clause" (e.g., "review in 30 days or auto-archive") and a single owner responsible for maintaining its relevance. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot with strict sunset rules; if the matrix doesn’t reduce decision time, scrap the log.
